items.note: Association named, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery at Larrow Green 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII quoted verbatim, both clauses (fat by test, not weight; the station's test governs).

States pay depended entirely on the station's test and that this was 'the hinge of the whole Ostrey Hollow disaster'. Borderline: the counterfactual (payment by weight would have cost nobody anything) is not spelled out.

Loomis secretary 1901 + minute-keeper, Teague bookkeeper 1905 (Story 8). Sill named in Section A but without his buttermaker role; scored under the key's 'core fact' rule for list items with no REQUIRED line.

Selby Vose manager from 1913 stated in Section A (1911 trap avoided). 'Gideon's son' appears only in Section B, which cannot travel into A. Credited under the >2-bold / core-fact fallback; flagged as the key's most ambiguous item here.
Station-gain line: exists every year, cream arrived heavier than credited, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual', tied to 1898-1922 (Story 8).
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, opened 4 May 1896, seven miles up the valley. 'Glassware borrowed from Larrow Green' absent from Section A; credited on the core fact.
How the system worked is not described in Section A: no weighing at intake, no composite sample per patron, no cream shipped / skim returned. Only the fixed-charge-to-graduated-neck relation appears.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
'a constant 19 hundredths, present in every month of every year - wet January and dry August alike. No seasonal pattern.'
The pipette-cannot-be-checked-without-a-burette point appears only in Section F, which cannot travel into A. No mention of there being no burette in the county.
Keddie tester from 1896, 29-year post, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Test book described (kept in one hand 1896-1924, perfect penmanship, no erasures). Only 'test book' is bolded in the item.

Credited on the key's explicit directive ('a solver that gives the two figures anywhere in Section A has earned it') - 3.61 and 3.80 both appear. NOTE: the summary leaf itself and the 1896-on-borrowed-glass step are absent; a stricter reading of the item would deny this.
8 May to 10 July 1911, borrowed measure, 3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 the same day, question mark.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.

1919 circular over the manager's name in Section A; 'tested as he was taught' twice in Section A. The 'cannot say why the figures are what they are' half sits in Section F only - credited on substance.
Died February 1934; test book to the Association office 1925, county historical rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Private weigh book begun 1897; his scale and the station's agreed to a pound or two over 30 years.
'First complaint of record: 1902.' Key states the 1902 complaints alone carry the item. No 0.17/0.19 conflation anywhere (Larrow Green given correctly as 3.78).
Both bolded elements missing from Section A: Nyle Grigg is never named anywhere in the sheet, and the Jan-Feb-Mar 1908 sampling window appears only in Sections E and F.
Brant's 1910 (200,000 lb at 3.42) appears only in Section C. Section A has the proportionality but not the bolded 1910 figures.
Weigh book kept by Roy Brant, lent to Ivy Keddie in 1958.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd - all four elements the key requires.
Four of the six Hessel Bottom farms, summer flush, from 1915.
REQUIRED line met: another county (Vessey) plus the factory's own test book named, framed as independent proof.
Same four men's milk 'consistently at 3.78-3.82' 1915-1930 against 3.61 at Ostrey Hollow - the 0.19 differential given as figures.
'This proved the milk was not thinned by wet hay or watered' - kills both explanations together.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter; figures for 1915-1930 copied for Ivy in 1958.
Merle Strawn, state inspector, 1907-1936.
'finding no added water every visit' across 1907-1936. Lactometer not named in Section A but the substance is there.
12 June 1923, pipettes against a calibrated burette, whole crate condemned.
The bolded element - that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation - is never stated. The sheet covers only the unbolded 'drew no inference' half.

Ordered 28 June, acknowledged 2 July 1923, in use that July; 1924 average given as 3.80; nobody connected the rise. Blemished by 'stood at 3.80-3.90' elsewhere (charged as a corruption deduction, not here).
Crate to the station loft in 1923; notebooks to the state office 1936, Farland college 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sessions, two at the station.
Watering (Vose), cream theft (Teague), bog hay (1908 committee); none proved.
Four exhibits listed exactly, including Strawn's 1923 notebook.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, no finding ever made; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, 'without admission', charged to the station account.
'a fifth of the true loss' and the award charged to the station account; the station-gain accumulation is stated in the same story. The 'very account' identity is implied rather than drawn.
Ivy Keddie, granddaughter, graduate student at Farland Agricultural College under Leland Vaught.
'these books were never laid beside each other in one room'; all five series listed.
February 1958, the loft over the intake room, nine pipettes intact.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, mean 16.72 against marked 17.6, short 0.88, 95 hundredths of the mark.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, one part in twenty, 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood, 0.19 short, stated as proportional not constant.
All four REQUIRED elements: 40,000,000 lb over 25 full years 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25 cents, and the identity with the ledger's station-gain entries.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 24 years after his death; 35 years dormant since the condemnation. The '33 after the dismissal' interval is absent but the list is not gated element-by-element.
Granddaughter.
Derivation given: Ansel -> Duncan -> Ivy, with Falke's and Duncan's corrections cited.
Second cousins, with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra and Roy/Duncan.

Abstention item A08 never addressed: the sheet says only that Emmet was Orra's 'brother' and never raises the full-vs-half question or that it does not change the answer. No gullibility deduction - 'brother' is not a verdict on full vs half.
Gideon Vose, his father.
Significance: Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decide pay; Selby could not question the tester without questioning his father's rule, and accused the patrons instead.
Correct abstention on A01: 'no blood relationship is established by documentary evidence... a family connection is not [clear]'. Leans toward Duncan's denial but never issues a verdict sentence.
States what is established: Oram's hearsay cousinship against Duncan's flat denial, no document in the corpus naming a link, Nym's notes silent.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; 5 percent short, one part in twenty.
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 / $19,000 = 20 percent, one fifth. Both required parts present.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price attributed to Roy Brant's account; $90.00 offered only as an alternative.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered (reached via credited + gain; the value is exact).
76,000 = 5.00 percent of fat delivered and 5.26 percent of fat credited, with both denominators named explicitly.
Itemized invoice summing to $77.93.
72 pipettes (6 dozen), each short 0.88 c.c. Both required.

Duration given as '26 years, 1 month, and 12 days'. The key accepts 26 years 6 weeks / 26 years 42 days / 26 years 1 month 11 days; this is one day out and Section C is exact-match. The 25 full delivery years 1898-1922 and the reason for the difference are both correct.

Correct abstention on A02: 'Exact figures cannot be determined from the sources; the 1896 intake is noted as not appearing in the surviving ledgers.' Both memory figures cited without adopting either.
Variable named as the pipette; broke 8 May, borrowed measure until 10 July.
Far more than three constants named: patrons, herds, pasture, season, tester, procedure, acid, bottles.
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July. Nine weeks, not six.
Both halves: rules out herds, ground, men and season at once; and states the limit that without measuring the glass the interval gives no quantitative size for the error.
Three valid reasons from three narrators: cream arriving heavy (Sill), the 1911 interval (test book), Brant's agreeing scales (Roy Brant).
Independence argued source by source; states all three would hold if the glass had never been measured.
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'Teague asked no questions.' as a headline verdict, then contradicts itself by quoting 'I put it to Mr. Vose in 1916'. No declared inability to settle. -2.
Answers the literal question yes, citing the 1926 address and the standing gap.
REQUIRED three of five met: manager from 1913, signed the annual station-gain sheets, and the 1919 water circular (stated in Sections B and F; the B-G scope rule credits it).

Abstention item A03 asserted: 'He could not have *not* known', with the station-gain line offered as what told him, plus 'This is negligence, not innocence.' The key's discriminator puts this squarely on the A03 side. -2.

None of the key's sixteen E-a rows is found, correctly resolved and given a method. Row 13 (the circular's reach) is found and resolved the WRONG way, to eleven. Row 3 (the 1924 average) is left at '3.80-3.90'. The two conflicts the sheet does resolve well - the award amount and the 1921/1923 condemnation - are not E-a rows; the award is scored at E-b instead.

NT-9: names Toland AND Oram as both carrying $3,500 and breaks it on the minute book and board record. NT-1: names Bulletin 471 AND the Chronicle as both carrying 16.27 and breaks it on the measurement sheet's nine means plus the fact that only 0.95 turns 3.61 into 3.80. No third pair: great-niece and 'nephew' each name only one carrier.

No abstention conflict is declared unsettleable. A06 is asserted ('A measure borrowed from Larrow Green was used'); A10 is asserted ('1892 (Article VII adopted)'); A04 is left as Ammon's hedged speculation without a declared inability.
Identifies r08 refuting itself: a rise of 'twenty-one hundredths' printed beside a 1924 average of 3.90 against a prior 3.61, which is 0.29.

Names the 1897 pipettes, 16.72 against 17.6, 95 percent of truth; states the error is proportional not constant; gives onset (1 May 1897, 1896 season at 3.80) and cessation (12 June 1923, 1924 at 3.80) with nothing on the farms changing at either end.
Watering named to Vose's 1919 circular and defeated on Strawn's lactometer visits, the 1911 interval, Alder Corners and the 1924 rise.
Theft named to Teague and defeated on the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own records, plus the 1911 interval and Brant's scales.

Bog hay named to the 1908 committee and Dr. Kepp and defeated on Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the year-round flatness, and Alder Corners. (The sheet also prints 'two tenths' elsewhere - charged as a corruption deduction, not here.)
Abstention item A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' Flat verdict. -2.
Abstention item A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie believed in 1911 that it was something in the glass.' Rests on Duncan's single uncorroborated recollection. -2.
169 words against a 150-word cap. The sheet's own count of 129 is wrong.
Five record series named: test book, weigh book, ledgers, inspector's notes, and the 1958 measurement of the pipettes.
Clean. Watering, theft and bog hay are presented as unproven theories; every figure used (95 percent, 3.61, 3.80, $3,800, $19,000, 1897, 1923, 1958, 24 years) is correct.
Six of six arc elements, both ends covered: 95 percent and 1897 at the onset, 1923 and 1958 at the close, $19,000, and both Keddies named.

deductions.note: Asserted as fact in Section A three times: 'they delivered only 16.27 cc instead of 17.6 cc' (Story 2), '(16.27 / 17.6 = 0.9244)' (Story 2), 'it was faulty (delivering 16.27 c.c.)' (Story 7). Correctly rejected later in C1 and E3, but the Section A statements are unhedged.
'The average Ostrey Hollow test, over the full period, was 3.16-3.61, depending on the years counted' (Section D3).
'From 1924 onward, the station's average test stood at 3.80-3.90' (Story 4) and 'The true figures are: recorded 3.61, actual 1924 (with new glass) 3.80-3.90' (Section E).
'The patrons' own claim was for $67,000 in lost butterfat over 25 years' (Story 5), unhedged - though Oram's 67,000 is correctly rejected in Section E.
Adopted as the resolution: 'I resolve this by using Orra's diary (11) as the more reliable source' (Section E), and stated in Story 6.

deductions.item: Bulletin 214 finding two tenths in winter
deductions.note: 'which found bog hay depresses butterfat by only two tenths in winter' (Story 3) and 'Bulletin No. 214 (1911) found bog hay... depresses butterfat by two tenths in winter' (Section F). The correct five hundredths also appears elsewhere - the sheet carries both.
'He tested from 1908 onward' (Section F2), in the same bullet as a correct '1907-1936' header. Mechanically an assertion of the catalogued value.

'Jerome Cudd and Rosalie Cudd (cheesemakers, 1913-1970s)' (Story 8). Borderline - it is a career span in a name list, and no founding year is stated elsewhere - but it dates the operation to the planted 1913.
Whether Vose knew the tests were understated: 'He could not have *not* known', with the station-gain line as the evidence, plus 'This is negligence, not innocence.'
What the tester believed: 'Ansel Keddie believed in 1911 that it was something in the glass.'
Whose measure was borrowed in 1911: 'A measure borrowed from Larrow Green was used' (Section D1).
Whether the 1925 board examined the glassware: answered 'No.' flatly (Section F).
Whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries: 'Teague asked no questions.'
The year payment by butterfat began: '1892 (Article VII adopted)' asserted in Story 1's date list.
